heading: Public methods coordinate
body:
A service or a controller has two kinds of methods. A public method is an entry point: a page, a route or another class calls it. A private method is a helper that only its own class calls. Tachyon asks each kind of method to do one job.

A public method only coordinates. It calls injected services and private methods, it stores or returns their results, and it builds models and values from them. It holds no `if`, `else`, `switch`, `match`, `when`, `guard` or ternary (`? :`). It holds no loop, no `&&`, `||`, `??`, `and` or `or`, and no `try` or `catch`. This includes the code of a lambda that the method writes. Kotlin's `?:` counts as a decision. Optional chaining such as `order?.total` and Rust's `?` operator are allowed.

A private method holds at most one decision or one loop. An `else if` chain is one decision, and an `&&` or `||` inside its condition is part of that decision. A private method that makes a decision does not call another private method that also makes a decision. A call such as `items.map(item => item.id)` is not a loop, because its lambda holds no decision. `items.filter(item => item.ready && item.shown)` is a loop.

The build refuses a service or a controller that breaks these rules with `TY1314`. The message names the method and the construct, and it shows how to write a private method in that language. `ty migrate check` lists every place to change.

| Language | Private method |
| --- | --- |
| JavaScript | A name that starts with `#`, such as `#pick(items)` |
| TypeScript | `private pick(items)` or `#pick(items)` |
| Python | A name that starts with `_`, such as `def _pick(self, items)` |
| Ruby | A method below `private` |
| PHP, Java, Kotlin, C# | A method with the `private` keyword |
| Swift | A method with `private` or `fileprivate` |
| Dart | A name that starts with `_` |
| Go | A method with a lowercase name |
| Rust | A method without `pub`. The methods of `impl Trait for Type` are public. |

In every language, a method whose name starts with `_` is private.

This check is new, so you can turn it off for one side of the app while you move code. For Tac services, set `tac.cohesion.check` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`. For Yon services and controllers, set `cohesion.check` to `false` in `server/application.json`. Use these settings only for migration.
